newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Summers calls for flexible forex policy globally.
newsitem.headline: Summers calls for flexible forex policy globally.

text.p: The easiest and most effective response to increased global capital flows is the adpotion of more flexible exchange rate policies, U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Friday.

"It is no accident that some of the otherwise well-managed economies that have had the least exchange rate flexibility have had the greatest difficulty in containing inflationary pressures," Summers told bankers in Singapore.
He said in a speech those economies were also most exposed to the risk of speculative attacks.
"The strong inflows that developing Asia has experienced in the past years have highlighted the risks and costs of insufficient exchange rate flexibility," Summers said.

He said he recognised the need for exchange rate policy in Asia to reflect historical and local conditions and, "I'm certainly not advocating any near-term momentous change in the policy of any country".
But he added that over time the necessary response to greater capital market integration is likely to be greater exchange rate flexibility.
This would provide policy-makers with a greater range of tools to manage capital inflows and outflows at a lower cost than is now the case.
"In our own case, we have found it best to pursue a strong dollar policy, based on strong economic fundamentals," he said.
"Our stance has been that the cost of resisting exchange rate movements driven by fundamentals has been high and ultimately, a waste," Summers said.
After his speech Summers was asked about the future direction of the long bond yield.

"I think I will stay out of making projections as to which way bond yields will go because I think that's appropriate in my position, and only offer you the observation that the Administration respects the independence of the Federal Reserve and does not prescribe what the Fed should do," Summers said.
